cells.tense: Here, with the pen, you are looking at the road while you walk it.
cells.act: cut through the inertia with one decisive act
cells.ask: Something in what you're pushing toward has been waiting on you. Do the smallest real piece of it — no more setups — and then leave the next hour alone.
cells.core:
You are moving toward something and you are looking at it as you go. That is not one skill being used on the other — the questions are what the motion runs on. You turn something over, ask what it actually is, and the next step shows itself. This is going well when the thing you're driving toward and the thing you're figuring out turn out to be the same thing, and today they do.

Something in what you are pushing toward has been waiting on you. Do the smallest real piece of it, without another setup. Then leave the next hour alone and watch what the doing does. Moving before you have finished understanding has a cost, and you will feel it. That cost is what the pace is made of. Take the step anyway.

cells.verb: to question, turn over, and look again at what is in front of you

cells.tense: By then the questions will already be ready for a room you haven't walked into.
cells.act: ask the beginner's question about where to go
cells.ask: Take a direction you're considering and ask about it the way a beginner would — before you know where it leads. Stop at the asking; nothing needs solving.
cells.core:
The questions are arriving early. Where you are driving, they come about a goal you have not reached, a turn you have not taken, and you turn them over anyway, looking for the shape of something that isn't there to be looked at yet. The curiosity is real and it is running. It has nothing solid to land on, so it circles — first question, second, third, none of them closing.

Take a direction you are considering and ask about it the way a beginner would, before you know where it leads. Stop at the asking. Nothing gets solved by it; the point is the asking, not the finding out. If you want a destination before you're allowed the question, that wanting is yours to sit with, not to organise.

cells.tense: You were curious about this path once, and you are still standing at the door you already passed.
cells.act: dream the next step and take it
cells.ask: Let what you're moving toward come to you before it's here — no questions, no working it out — and take the first step that arrives from that.
cells.core:
The questions that used to open something up have stopped arriving. Where you are moving, the road is already known — you have been over it, you know what it looks like, and there is nothing left in it to turn over. What you know is solid. The room around it has gone quiet.

Let what you are moving toward come to you before it is here. No questions, no working it out — sit with it once this week and let yourself feel forward into it. Then take the first step that comes out of that. If it feels like a waste of a good hour, that is fine. Nothing has to come of it. You are not trying to want the not-yet; you are letting it be there again.

cells.tense: The questions are being asked and answered, and the day is credited with carrying you.
cells.act: weigh what it costs them against what it gives
cells.ask: Somewhere this week you decided what was fair without noticing the deciding. Say the two sides — what it gives someone and what it costs them — and own the call as yours.
cells.core:
You keep asking good questions where you are headed, and if someone described your week you would not put your name on it. The curious ones, the ones who turn things over instead of deciding early — that is already how you move toward what you want. What goes unaccounted for is the judging underneath: calls about what is fair, whose turn it is, what to carry, made all week without noticing who was making them.

Somewhere this week you decided what was fair without noticing the deciding. Say the two sides — what it gives someone and what it costs them — and own the call as yours. It may be smaller than it feels. It may be exactly the size you thought. Either way you get to see your hand in it, which is different from taking it back.
cells.sheetLine: You ask the sharp questions and file the verdicts under nothing.

attempts.check: The core says something is being organised before it has been felt; the record supports organising feeling as a balanced act, not the speed, so a reader could reasonably say that reading is invention and trim it. The ask still stands if the read is wrong: the next hard thing that arrives is there to be noticed either way, and the person can answer it without accepting my account of them. The sentence that serves me more than the person is 'you are bracing at a future that can't be written in' — it is a phrase with a nice ring, and it tells them nothing they can use.
